description: External, versioned access policy for the knowledge-graph PoC and the authorization trust boundary's source of truth. Kept OUTSIDE the graph and versioned separately from both the data and the ontology. Authorization is two-dimensional: role-based capability grants (which sensitivity CATEGORIES of fields, which ENTITIES, and whether aggregates are allowed) plus CLEARANCE (gated against each node's in-graph `classification` for row-level visibility). An identity may optionally mark categories as `clearanceGatedCategories`: those fields are redacted per-row on classified rows above its clearance instead of the whole row being hidden, so the row stays visible (and counts in aggregates) while the gated fields are protected. The `catalog` is the curated, queryable surface the structured-intent query builder validates typed queries against; a field absent from the catalog is queryable by no one (default-deny).

Aircraft.description: The aircraft (airframe) the knowledge graph describes.

Specification.description: Published performance specifications and limits for the aircraft type.

Aerodrome.description: Reference catalogue of every aerodrome (airport) that appears in the network the aircraft operates in. This is NOT a record of where this aircraft has flown — listing aerodromes here says nothing about which the aircraft departed from or flew to (that is route data, held only on Flight). `icao` is its ICAO code (e.g. EGGD); a Flight's departureAerodrome/destinationAerodrome hold these codes, so map a flight aerodrome code to a name by matching it to an Aerodrome's `icao`.

System.description: A major aircraft system (e.g. airframe, electrical, powerplant).

Component.description: A maintainable component or part fitted to the aircraft.

PistonEngine.description: The aircraft's piston engine (the powerplant), a specialised component.

Document.description: A maintenance or reference document (manual, AD, service bulletin). Only metadata lives in the graph (it acts as the index): the document body is stored externally and fetched backend-side via the document tool, NOT through a graph query. Reading the body requires the `document` sensitivity category; an identity without it can still see a document exists and its title/version but not its text. The body is never a graph field, so it is absent from this catalog by design.

Flight.description: A flight flown by the aircraft. Duration fields are maintenance-relevant; route fields (departure/destination/distance/altitude) are restricted; whole classified (e.g. military) flights are gated by clearance. departureAerodrome is the ICAO code the flight took off from; destinationAerodrome is the ICAO code it landed at — an aerodrome counts as one the aircraft 'flew to'/'landed at' only when it is some flight's destinationAerodrome, while 'departed from'/'took off from' means departureAerodrome.

WorkItem.description: A unit of engineering work (e.g. a feature or task) tracked through the SDLC.

PullRequest.description: A proposed code change submitted for review and merge.

Hazard.description: An identified safety hazard arising from a system, addressed by the safety process.

SystemRequirement.description: A system-level requirement allocated to an aircraft system.

SoftwareRequirement.description: A software requirement derived from a system requirement, carrying an assurance (DAL) level.

TestResult.description: The outcome of executing a test (PASSED/FAILED).

ReleaseBaseline.description: A configuration-controlled release baseline of the software installed on the aircraft.

ComplianceClaim.description: A claim of compliance with a certification objective, supported by evidence.

Evidence.description: A piece of assurance evidence produced by verification or analysis.

AssuranceCase.description: A structured assurance case that assures a release baseline.

CodeModule.description: A source code module (with commit and version) implementing a software component.

InterfaceRequirement.description: A requirement governing an interface used by an aircraft system.

PipelineRun.description: An execution of a CI/CD pipeline that runs tests for a change.

StaticAnalysisResult.description: The outcome of static analysis run against a code module.

SafetyControl.description: A control that mitigates a hazard, implemented by software.

Defect.description: A defect found during verification, resolved by a code change.

ConfigurationItem.description: A configuration-managed item deployed on an aircraft system.

TestCase.description: A defined test case that verifies a software requirement.

ReviewRecord.description: A record of a code or pull-request review.

SoftwareComponent.description: A software component that realises an aircraft system's software.

ArchitectureElement.description: An element of the software architecture that satisfies requirements.

CertificationObjective.description: A certification objective (e.g. a DO-178C objective) a claim demonstrates compliance with.

ChangeRequest.description: A request for change that raises work items and affects requirements.

Actor.description: A person or team involved in the engineering lifecycle (author, reviewer, owner, assignee).

AFFECTS.description: A change request affects a software requirement, or a defect affects a software component.

ALLOCATED_TO.description: A system requirement is allocated to the aircraft system it constrains.

ANALYSES.description: A static-analysis result analyses a code module.

APPROVES.description: An actor approves an assurance case.

ARRIVES_AT.description: A flight arrives at an aerodrome.

ASSIGNED_TO.description: An actor (person or team) is assigned to a work item or certification objective.

ASSURES.description: An assurance case assures a release baseline.

AUTHORED.description: An actor authored a pull request.

CLAIMS_COMPLIANCE_WITH.description: A compliance claim claims compliance with a certification objective.

DEPARTS_FROM.description: A flight departs from an aerodrome.

DEPLOYED_ON.description: A configuration item is deployed on an aircraft system.

DERIVES_FROM.description: A software or interface requirement derives from a higher-level system requirement.

ENDANGERS.description: A safety hazard endangers an aircraft system.

EXECUTES.description: A pipeline run executes a test case.

FEEDS.description: A system or component feeds another component.

FITTED_TO.description: A component fitted to another component.

FOUND_BY.description: A defect was found by a test result.

FUELS_FROM.description: A component fuels from another component.

GOVERNED_BY.description: An aircraft, system or specification is governed by a reference document.

HAS_AD.description: The aircraft has an airworthiness directive document.

HAS_CONFIGURATION_ITEM.description: A release baseline has a configuration item.

HAS_CONTROL_SURFACE.description: A component has control surface another component.

IMPLEMENTED_BY.description: A safety control is implemented by a software component; a work item is implemented by a pull request.

IMPLEMENTS.description: A code module implements a software component, or a software component implements an architecture element.

IMPLEMENTS_WORK.description: A work item implements (delivers) a software component.

INCLUDED_IN_BASELINE.description: A software component is included in a release baseline.

INCLUDES_CLAIM.description: An assurance case includes a compliance claim.

INSTALLED_ON.description: A software release baseline is installed on the aircraft.

MEMBER_OF.description: An actor is a member of a team.

MERGES.description: A pull request merges a code module.

MITIGATES.description: A safety control mitigates a hazard.

MOUNTED_ON.description: A component mounted on another component.

OWNED_BY.description: A software component is owned by an actor (person or team).

POWERED_BY.description: A component is powered by a system or another component.

PRODUCES.description: A test case produces a test result; a test result or static-analysis result produces assurance evidence.

PROVIDES_IGNITION_TO.description: A component provides ignition to another component.

RAISES.description: A change request raises a work item.

REALISES.description: A software component realises (provides the software for) an aircraft system.

RESOLVES.description: A pull request resolves a defect.

REVIEWS.description: A review record reviews a code module or pull request.

SATISFIES.description: An architecture element or software component satisfies a requirement.

TRACES_TO_HAZARD.description: A software requirement traces to the hazard it addresses.

TRIGGERS.description: A pull request triggers a pipeline run.

USES_EVIDENCE.description: A compliance claim uses a piece of assurance evidence.

USES_INTERFACE.description: An interface requirement governs an interface used by an aircraft system.

VERIFIES.description: A test case verifies a software requirement.

identities.description: Default identity for unknown or unselected users. Least privilege: basic reference data about the aircraft, its published specifications, and aerodromes. No maintenance history, no flight durations, no flight routes, no aggregates. Unrecognised user ids resolve to this identity (default-deny).

Maintains the airframe, engine and components. Sees flight durations, maintenance history (components, documents, performance) and the routes of ordinary flights, and may run aggregates. Classified (e.g. military) flights stay visible as records and count toward totals such as flying hours, but their route (departure/destination/distance/altitude) is redacted.

Operations role cleared to the highest level. May see everything maintenance can, PLUS flight routes, aerodrome coordinates, and classified (e.g. military) flights that other identities cannot see at all.

Engineering identity for the software development lifecycle. Sees the engineering domain (requirements, implementation, verification, assurance, safety, configuration, work management and the people/teams involved) plus basic operational facts about the aircraft and its systems. Cannot see flights, routes, durations, maintenance or document content.
